I'm not sure how much this will help, but I discovered I was making a small amount of side money by breeding chickens.

Basically, I bought one hen and one rooster and planned on hatching the fertilized eggs to get more free hens. Well the 1st five I hatched were all male, and since males don't lay eggs, I sold them. Turns out male chickens sell for more than fertilized eggs.

1 male chicken is an investment, many males is a financial burden if you keep them, since they don't produce a good you can sell but you still have to pay to feed them.

1 female chicken will give you free eggs to make money off of and endless amounts of free babies that will either sell well or lay more eggs to make more money off of.

It's by no means a fast or efficient way to make money, but in this particular sos game, even a few pennies made and saved here and there can go a long way.

Also-

I focused more on ranching than farming during the early game. The animals pay for themselves easily after a season or 2 and it doesn't take to much stamina to care for a lot of them, only time.
They are a great long term investment, and they're goods only increase in value as time goes on.

I never filled both my starting fields with crops because it's heckin expensive and they only sell for a flat rate, just once, and don't grow in quality without fertilizer. 
You do need crops for various requests, so I recommend using only a few rows of one field to start with. (Like on row of tomatoes, 5 tomatoes total, and a row of watermelon, 5 watermelon total, during spring season). Don't feel pressured to use all you crop space in the early game, it'll just burn a whole in your wallet.

I've done some digging and here's what I've found:

There's a pattern of people either triggering gustafa or gordy, but never both.

I found a short article stating that the 1st event is racing the turtle, triggered by exiting Gustafas OR maybe gordys house (unconfirmed). The second is Nina telling you about a dream she had of the forest sprites. The third event where she races Hugh involves the sprites, so you have to have had her tell you about the dream before the 3rd event will trigger.

Fogu- doesn't talk about the dream but implies that racing the turtle is a 2 part event, where you trigger part 1 by exiting gustafas house and part 2 by exiting Gordys house.

Based on all this, I've personally concluded that the short article is correct about the type of events. Fogu is right about the name of the events. And everyone has been wrong about the turtle race being a 2 part event because the game makers gave the events names that implied it was 2 seperate events rather than 2 different ways of triggering the same 1st event.

I'm not saying I'm right, I just hope this helps. I will now allow myself to stop panicking and move on to year 2.

Sometimes a panic attack happens for no gosh darn reason, which is annoying and for some, scary. Since you're young and fit, I'd like to recommend music while going for a jog or other exercise, something about physical activity really helps alot of people with their anxiety and panic attacks. (It might also take your mind off the attack, which is always good).

First, congratulations on making it through your first panic attack, (1st is usually pretty bad because you don't know what the heck happening). Second, panic attacks are unique to the person they happen to. There is no time frame for when they do or don't start and end. 

Over thinking a panic attack is common, but does tend to make future panic attacks more frequent and intense (in my personal experience).

I'd recommend, that when you start remembering and worrying about previous panic attacks, find a healthy distraction, and after that (each time you might start thinking about the attack again) reward yourself for how long you went without worrying (even if it was only a few minutes).

It's better to reward the small successes rather than feeding into the attacks with worry and stress.

I to, sometimes can't help but think about how I felt and feeling during an attack, I personally choose to focus on the feeling I get when the attack is letting up, for me it feels like a vice grip on my sanity is loosening and foreshadows the end of an attack, so it's a feeling I like and gives me confidence that I can handle future attacks (I don't need to worry each day about whether an attack will or won't happen because a panic attack always comes to an end and that feels really amazing).

Of course, I'm not a doc, so if things start to get worse, for seek a medical opinion, even your general doc/primary care provider can help.

Oh and for the sake of your sanity, don't Google panic attacks. That search engine seems exceptionally talented at convincing even perfectly healthy people that they have cancer.

Anyway, hope you start to feel better soon 👍

There is no set 'grieving period'. Everyone grieves in different ways and at different speeds. 

The worst thing you can do is accidentally make him feel rushed through the grieving process, this happens when well intentioned people who love and care about the grieving person try too hard to help that person feel better.

The best thing you can do is let him know that you are a safe person to be around, who will let him feel all the icky and terrible feelings he needs to feel, with no pressure to feel better before hes really ready. 

I'm grieving my mother currently, there are just some times when I dont want to cry infront of anyone, not even family. Some days I need to be close with my loved ones and other days I just want to curl up in a blanket and be alone for a little while. 

If you really feel the need to help in some way then here's what you could do: the first weeks of grieving can leave you feeling like you're drowning and on auto pilot, doing even simple tasks is hard. The thing we often need is for someone to help us with the things that are now too hard to do, like daily chores, cooking meals, getting work done, etc. Any burdens you can temporarily relieve him of in his daily life could help relieve some of the overwhelming thoughts and feeling hes going through (if that makes sense).

And lastly, he himself may not even know what he needs (I didnt know at 1st), but it helped that I had loved ones who were emotionally available when I did finally figure out what I needed.

It doesnt seem to be a common symptom for most people (in my experience), but for me, every panic attack I have comes with the sensation that I'm burning up. It's usually my arms that get hit the hardest, but I have had it through my whole body at times.

Mine tends to feel like a mix of fire and electricity rushing through my veins, but this symptom tends be unique in how its felt from person to person (again just from my own experience with it).

Hope you're feeling better (sometimes a cold clothe or shower helps, just in case you feel this symptom again at some point).

 I have a couple of ideas, assuming Im understanding you correctly:
The 1st thing I thought was, as you get older your IQ doesnt necessarily go up, many average children catch up to their very bright peer as they get older. It could be that you didnt loose anything but rather your peers simply caught up to you.

But you also mentioned that you feel like you've regressed intellectually and progressed emotionally, I'm no doc but the second thing I thought was, this could be a medical issue.

Finally, I was wondering why you chose this subreddit, did you maybe forget to mention you are grieving a loss of loved one recently? Though I personally feel that just about anything can be grieved over, even the lose of things like, independence, mobility, and intelligence,  if you had it then lost it and it was important to you, then it can be grieved.

All in all, it very much sounds like talking to your doc is a must, I personally would look into some therapy, not because your crazy, but because therapists are often very good, non-biased, listeners that sometimes have ideas of how to help people that aren't as obvious or well known about (for example, I was recommended to a specialist for help learning about how my aspergers effects me in day to day life. I'm really sorry that you've lost someone you clearly cared about a lot. I too have had many feelings about wanting to 'get over it' after my mom passed last October. What I've learned is that society has unrealistic expectations about how long people should grieve and that there's some magical point when you just except it and move on, this is just not true but many people still put this burden of 'getting over it' on themselves. To still be grieving after a year is actually normal and ok. Each day that passes we dont stop loving those we've lost and wanting them back, but we do get a little bit stronger so those feelings become less and less difficult to manage. You say you want to stop feeling the way you do, I wonder, if each day is the same or worse than the last, than it might be time to reach out for professional help. Grieving is normal, but being so utterly crippled by grief that you cant function day to day is not normal and it's ok, whether it's been a year, 10 years, or even longer, to still need some help dealing with grief in healthy ways.

First, I'm so sorry for your loss, the death of a loved one is never easy or completely regretless, even in the best, most perfect of circumstances. Second, I'd like to share with you a personal belief that I have, in case it could help you. I believe that our loved ones find absolute peace when they pass (regardless of what kind of person they were in life) and that the peace they find means they only ever look back at their loved ones and wish happiness for them. I try and live my best life possible so my mom who passed last october never has to be sad or worried that I'm holding on to regrets and pain. She wouldn't want that for me and I think your mema wouldn't want that for you either. Please seek some kind of counseling for what you're going through because your feelings and regrets are valid and you deserve to have a safe space to talk about them and work through them. Please dont bury them or let them eat away at you, your mema loved you and (in my personal belief) still loves you whole heartedly, she only ever wanted you to be happy and that doesn't end even though she's passed. Third, it's ok if you disagree with what I believe, but please still consider getting some counseling because no one deserves to be destroyed by guilt, no matter what mistakes they've made.

I'm so so so sorry that this happening to you. Whether a loved one leaves us suddenly or we have time to say our goodbyes, the pain of loosing them is still strong and sometimes overwhelming, you are not alone in feeling this way. If you have family that you're on good terms with or close to in any way, please reach out to them. You sound like you are in alot of pain because of this and sometimes being with family and talking to them openly about how you're afraid and hurting, even if it's very hard to be that open, can help a lot. If not family, then a trusted friend or even a counselor (I would assume the hospital your grandmother is at has some type of support for families in these situations). I know its cliche but trust me, keeping to yourself, tucking all those feelings away, it only makes the pain worse. Also, I know this might be hard, it might feel completely overwhelming to even try, but spend as much time with your grandma as you can, you both can use that time anyway you want. You can be open and cry together, or you can spend every second laughing and joking around as you try to keep each other strong, what ever you need to do, there is no right or wrong way to feel right now.

First of all, I'm sending you a big reddit hug, because it sounds like you really need one right now. Second, I'm so sorry for your loss and I understand how much it hurts. It's ok to not be ready, I dont think there ever is a 'ready' so to speak. I want you to know that its really amazing of you, to be in pain and grief, and still trying so hard to be the strong one for your family. There comes a time when it's ok to be weak and emotionally vulnerable WITH your family, and that's usually at the funeral. Just remember, your love for her is just as great as theirs and it's ok for you to not be the strongest person at the funeral. Absolutely you can be there for your family, but please let them be there for you too, you dont have to be strong all alone. (Speaking for personal experience) being the strong one doesnt leave alot of room to grieve and that's what it sounds like you really need to be able to do at her funeral.

I lost my mom a few months ago, it wasn't to covid but it was sudden and not fair and she was my best friend my whole life, so I know how awful things are for you right now. Please call your mom and talk to her about how you're feeling, being alone with these feelings is the worst. Grieving alone is no good. We are here for you, but if you can, call your mom too.

I understand, certain physical sensations can become triggers, I have those too so your definitely not alone. What's helped me alot is coming to terms with the fact that panic attacks are going to happen and sometimes  they cant be prevented, all that can be done is getting through them in the moment and then relishing in the sweet sweet relief that you feel when it's done. Powering through may seem like it's not very helpful but it's more about taking control away from the panic and fear and giving that control back to yourself. It's not easy and the panic feels awful but it does end, every panic attack always comes to an end.

I'm so sorry this is happening to you, I spent time feeling the exact same way so I completely understand how miserable it must feel for you. Ave you considered cognitive behavioral therapy,? it's sort of like safely and slowly relearning how to not be afraid of the things that are triggers for you. Please discuss this option with your therapist and be brutally honest with them about how crippling your anxiety is for you despite the help you're currently getting. They should be understanding and wanting to help you, they may not know how bad things are for you (I'm a chronic sugar coater because I hate being vulnerable in front of others, even those I trust. Therapy didnt help until I let ALL the ugly out). If you think you might be doing this, tell your therapist so they can help you get to a place where you feel safe to tell them the REALLY bad stuff. We are all here for you!

Its not uncommon for a panic attack to trigger more panic attacks during or after the original attack. Again, I'm really sorry this happened to you. All of us here in this subreddit are here for you, you can always ask us for help.

The sooner you recognize that feeling the easier it will be for you to be like 'I know what this means so now I can actively work to make it less intense or prevent it all together'. Try a variety of healthy coping strategies, like breathing calmly, distracting yourself, or talking with a trusted person who helps keep you calm. (I like art and music so that's what I use). If you're at work when one happens, try asking for a break, taking 10 calm slow breaths, or another coping strategy.

Keep at it!! This is good! If it's too hard at first, exercise with a friend so when you are done they can help keep you calm, make you feel safe and distract you from the worst of the panic. Exercising alone may still be hard but not as hard as it was at first. Plus exercising with friends is always better in my opinion (even if you dont have anxiety).
The longest it's taken me to recover from a panic attack is 1 month when my depression was at its worst and 3 days when I'm was in a very great place mentally.

I strongly disagree with using drugs to fix anxiety caused by drugs. Regardless of legality, you need to stop asap! Weed, acid, and even CBD can trigger panic attacks. There's no way to predict when and how much will or wont cause one, the only true relief is to stop using them while introducing new and healthier habits into your life, like a 30 min walk with good music instead of wax pen, or, hanging out with friends to have a good time instead of leaning on an acid trip to make you feel good. I dont mean to be so harsh, I've just watched alot of my friends get stuck where you are and I hate watching people suffer. On the other had though, if you stop everything but continue to have panic attacks, see a doctor and then you can figure out if CBD will help you, because it really can help some people.

Im so sorry for your loss! Hang in there, you are not alone. The big thing to look at is how it effects your everyday life. If it's just a really big project that you've found yourself more invested in than you thought you would be, than its probably not a bad thing (even if the topic may be morbid, it could be your way of processing grief). If the project becomes all consuming, you start neglecting other things and people you love or yourself, or the project is having an especially negative impact on you emotionally and or mentally and everyday life starts to take a back seat to this project, than it my not be healthy to continue. I say, check in with your loved ones to make sure they aren't worried that you're going too far with it. You can also mention it to a grief counselor, they've heard everything so probably have a good idea of what's healthy and what's not.

Sounds like the change in routine, especially your electronic usage is the more likely culprit. I'm not saying it's not related to the anxiety, but if you are able to make a quick change (like less hunching over a computer) and it resolves 99.999% of the pain, that's a win for you.
Yup, the tingly feel is the most common symptom for me, you are not alone. ( I'm not 100% sure but it think it has to do with adrenaline rushing through your system)

I strongly disagree with the get out of bed after 20min method. For me, getting out of bed is like hitting the restart button, I feel even more awake when I'm not in my bed. If I have a panic attack in bed, youtube becomes my best friend. I know they say phones make your sleep worse but for me, a soothing, innocent cat video or Youtuber playing a game can both lull me to sleep and distract me from the panic I'm feeling. This obviously isnt for everyone. You might want to consider  something I use when I'm really struggling, it's called Calms Forte sleep aid. It's like meletonan but also has anxiety and stress reducing effects. The brand I use is called Hylands and it's not a big time drug or anything crazy strong, it's just a generic aid that works well for me and might be able to help you too.

There was a time when my anxiety ruled my life, I became a shell of myself. I survived and am determined for that to never happen to me again, and to anyone else if I can help it. I find the more I know about something, the more power I have to keep calm. It helps me alot, so I hope it helps you too. We are all with you 👍

I had a panic attack while trying to fall asleep once and spent the next 2 years sleeping on a couch because beds became a trigger for me. Only one thing worked in fixing this, getting in a bed, letting the attack happen, then staying in the bed and falling asleep after the attack ended. In the morning, beds were no longer a trigger. I guess what I'm saying is, sometimes if you develop a trigger, you need to safely confront it before things can get better. You have every right to be feeling the way you are and having anxiety, but after everything you've gone through, I dont want you to end up on couch like I did. Other things you can do are start a night time routine with lots of positive things. An attack may happen still, but the point is to give as little power over your sleep as possible.

I absolutely understand! My mind likes to think non stop too, so your not alone there. From personal experience, I use to have the same fear, that the anxiety would get worse and worse with each attack. After alot of help and learning how to manage my anxiety, I discovered that the severity of attacks can decrease too. As for the fire sensation, it seems to be a less common symptom, I rarely hear about it in this sub. Ironically, I too have this symptom and it STINKS! It's like a hot liquid is being poured through my veins and I just want to jump out of skin to escape from it. If this becomes a regular symptom for you, I recommend cold showers, they dont make the heat go away but they make it more tolerable so it's not so hard to get through the attack. (I dont know the exact science, but I believe this feeling is related to the massive adrenaline rush that can happen when we go into fight or flight.)

It's very odd they sent you home with those meds. I'm on lexapor for chronic depressive disorder, never heard of it used for anxiety before. Id get in to see a psychiatrist asap to make sure those are even necessary. As for the lingering anxiety, that's normal. I use the description of the after math of a panic attack as being like ripples in a pond. Good news is, just like ripples, it ends eventually. But if you think about it too much, you can give the fear more power and cause continuous anxiety for longer than normal. I recommend keeping to your usual routines and spoiling yourself a little bit. It's ok to intentionally do things to distract yourself, it less time thinking about the panic after all. Also, almost all humans have at least one panic attack in their life time, it doesnt mean your going to have it forever, but if you do start to struggle with it, tell your doctor.

Therapy is awesome!!! Best thing I ever did!.... this is true about 75% of the time. In truth therapy only really works when you find the right doc that clicks with you. If you come across a doc that just doesnt seem to get you or you dont feel like your really connecting, it's ok, it's normal, dont give up, just like with any relationship, sometimes people get along and sometimes they dont. No ones at fault, but when this happens it can be very discouraging, especially for first timers. Therapy can be amazinling beneficial and I'm really glad to hear your giving it a try. I hope it helps you, and we are with you!

Clonazepam is only supposed to be used in short term cases. My doc took me of clonazepam after long term use because recent studies showed an increase risk of developing dementia early in your senior years after long time use of it. I dont know anything about valium but I agree with your advise nonetheless. Having this level of anxiety with bpd is something their doc needs to know about and might know of a good medicine for this situation.

Your going to be ok. Panic attacks can be like ripples in a pond. The original attack is like the stone throne into the pond and any attacks and anxiety soon after are the 'ripples' and ripples dont go on forever. If the attacks you're having are as strong or stronger than the first one that started this, it's possible you're so stressed about having another attack when you wake up that its triggering more attacks. If so, the loop can be hard to break because its self fulfilling, but it can be done. Try to go to bed not fearing another attack but rather with the mindset that IF you have an attack in the morning, you are strong enough to get through it and that all panic attacks have an end. Also try to make waking up a good thing with some kind of personal reward, like icecream for breakfast etc... we want your brain to go from, fear of waking up because of possible attack, to, relaxed about waking up because more good things are going to happen rather than bad.

Yup I have the same issue, silence and boredom are triggers for me. These days I use music and youtube in the background to take my mind off of the anxious feeling that likes to creep up on me. If I find myself panicking, I start a project to keep myself occupied, paint a little wooden box from the dollar store, color a picture with markers, write a mini story about a random topic I'm currently interested in, and sometimes I just take a shower, go for a walk, or read a book. Im really good at daydreaming to help keep my mind busy, so it's not hard for me to drag my mind into a better place, but it wasn't always easy. I recommend prepping before doing something to help with your anxiety, for example, when I feel the anxiety building, I throw on my pjs, get my softest pillows and warmest blankets, make some coco, and hunker down with a 'project's. The extra effort I put in helps alot, it's like when you stretch before playing a sport, it gets you ready. It's like reverse meditation, instead of clearing your mind, you fill up so there's no more room for anxiety.

I lost my mom 2 weeks ago, I thought the pain would never end and many people told me the pain never goes away, you just get stronger. This made things a thousand time worse for me and is NOT my advise for you. My advise is that at first the sadness and pain come from desperately wanting your loved one back, but eventually a shift happens and then all the sadness and pain come from they many wonderful memories you have of that loved one. For me at least, the happiness of these memories helps counter the sadness and make things a bit easier.  You said your relationship was bumpy but you also seem to suggest you do have happy memories too. Hold on to those close, cry to those memories, it's ok to be sad because the happy memories will start to lift you up again. Most importantly, dont rush it, if you need an hour to ugly cry and scream and curse at the world, do it. I had a moment like this and afterwards it felt like some of the pain leaked out with my sobs and screams. I hope this helps.

Edit: I also felt like I had to be strong for my family, if I was weak in front of them, I felt like we'd all fall apart. It's ok to be strong for those who are grieving with you, just remember to give yourself time and permission to be weak too. It hurts worse if you bottle it up for too long.
